rules.title: Lease Termination Due to Domestic Violence
rules.requirement: Victims of domestic violence may terminate their lease without penalty prior to the expiration of the lease by providing the landlord with written notice and specified documentation. Lease termination takes effect on the 30th day following landlord's receipt of notice and documentation, with rent prorated up to termination date.
rules.summary_plain: If you are a victim of domestic violence, you can end your lease early without penalty by giving your landlord written notice and proof of the violence. Your lease ends 30 days after your landlord gets your notice, and you only pay rent up to that date.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si usted es víctima de violencia doméstica, puede terminar su contrato de arrendamiento antes de tiempo sin penalización entregando a su arrendador un aviso por escrito y prueba de la violencia. Su contrato termina 30 días después de que el arrendador reciba su aviso, y solo paga la renta hasta esa fecha.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to all residential leases except transient or seasonal rentals.
rules.exemptions_text: Transient or seasonal rentals are exempt.
rules.quoted_span: victims of domestic violence may terminate their lease without penalty prior to the expiration of the lease by providing the landlord with a written notice that the tenant or a child of the tenant faces an imminent threat of serious physical harm from a specific person, (that must be identified in the written notice) , if the tenant remains on the premises, and by fulfilling any of the following requirements

rules.title: Return of Security Deposit After Lease Termination Due to Domestic Violence
rules.requirement: Within 15 business days after lease termination due to domestic violence, the landlord must make the security deposit plus any interest available to the tenant or agent, and notify the tenant in writing within 3 business days when and where to pick it up. The deposit must be available for 30 days during normal business hours.
rules.summary_plain: If you end your lease because of domestic violence, your landlord must return your security deposit and interest within 15 business days and tell you when and where to pick it up within 3 business days.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si termina su contrato debido a violencia doméstica, su arrendador debe devolver su depósito de seguridad e intereses dentro de 15 días hábiles y decirle cuándo y dónde recogerlo dentro de 3 días hábiles.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies when lease is terminated under the Safe Housing Act due to domestic violence.
rules.quoted_span: Within 15 business days after the lease  is terminated, the landlord shall make available the return of the tenant’s security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant’s agent. In addition, within three business days after the lease is terminated, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of when and where the tenant can pick up the security deposit.

rules.title: Lease Termination for Disabled Tenants
rules.requirement: A disabled tenant may terminate the lease if the unit is not handicapped accessible and the landlord refuses or is unable to make the unit accessible after request.
rules.summary_plain: If you have a disability and your landlord refuses or cannot make your unit accessible, you can end your lease.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si tiene una discapacidad y su arrendador se niega o no puede hacer que su unidad sea accesible, puede terminar su contrato de arrendamiento.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to tenants with disabilities requesting accessibility modifications.
rules.quoted_span: New Jersey State Law also allows a disabled tenant to terminate the lease agreement if the unit is not handicapped accessible. A lease can be terminated if the landlord refuses to make the unit handicapped accessible after the tenant requests that the unit be made handicapped accessible and the landlord is unable or unwilling to do so
